cases.name: repo rrv.ini
cases.ini:
# =============================================================================
# RRV-Recomp launch settings.
#
# `./run.sh` (no arguments) reads this file. Edit a value, save, launch.
# Command-line flags still win over this file for that one launch, e.g.
#     ./run.sh --scale 2
# Use a different file with:   ./run.sh --config /path/to/other.ini
#
# Format: `key = value`, one per line. Lines starting with # or ; are comments.
# Do NOT put a comment after a value on the same line.
# A key that is commented out or deleted uses its built-in default (shown in
# each entry as "default:"). Booleans accept: true/false, yes/no, on/off, 1/0.
# =============================================================================


[display]
# --- ratio ------------------------------------------------------------------
# REAL widescreen. The game's camera renders a wider view (shows more of the
# scene at the sides) and the window shows it at that shape.
# This changes guest data (an RR5 enhancement). 4:3 is the stock game.
#   4:3 | 16:9 | 16:10 | 21:9
# default: 16:9
ratio = 16:9

# --- hud --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only matters when ratio is not 4:3. How the 2D parts (HUD, menus, text)
# behave on a wide picture.
#   stretch : never fixed; 2D is stretched wide (what the No.47 hack shows)
#   fixed   : 2D keeps 4:3 proportions, pinned to the screen edges, everywhere
#   race    : fixed during races only; menus stay stretched
#   (no47 is accepted as an alias for stretch)
# default: stretch
hud = stretch

# --- aspect -----------------------------------------------------------------
# How the finished picture fits the window. Presentation only, the guest does
# not change. Leave EMPTY to follow `ratio` (recommended).
#   (empty) | auto | 4:3 | 16:9 | 16:10 | 21:9 | stretch
#   auto    : 4:3 with black bars
#   stretch : fill the whole window (distorts if the window shape differs)
# default: empty
aspect =

# --- window -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Starting window size in pixels, WIDTHxHEIGHT (for example 1920x1080).
# Leave EMPTY for automatic: 80% of the screen height, at the picture's shape.
# default: empty
window =

# --- fullscreen -------------------------------------------------------------
# Start in fullscreen. F11 toggles it while the game runs.
#   true | false
# default: false
fullscreen = false

# --- integer_scaling --------------------------------------------------------
# Snap the picture to whole-number multiples of its size (sharper, but bars
# around it if the window is not an exact multiple).
#   true | false
# default: false
integer_scaling = false

# --- present_pacing ---------------------------------------------------------
# Even frame pacing: every frame is shown for the same time, so motion is
# smooth (without it, frames can stay up 8 or 25 ms instead of 16.7 ms on a
# 120 Hz Mac screen: judder). Costs about 6-9 ms of extra display delay.
# Presentation only, the guest does not change. Takes effect on restart.
#   true | false
# default: true
present_pacing = true


[rendering]
# --- render_mode ------------------------------------------------------------
#   full  : full-frame rendering at 448+ real rows, progressive ~59.94 Hz.
#           Needs a full-capable runtime (the default runtime is one).
#   field : the older half-height field output (Gate-4 style).
# default: full
render_mode = full

# --- scale ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal resolution multiplier, full mode only. Higher = sharper, slower GPU.
#   2 | 4
# default: 4
scale = 4

# --- aa1 --------------------------------------------------------------------
# PCSX2's AA1 edge anti-aliasing emulation (full mode).
#   true | false
# default: true
aa1 = true

# --- fxaa -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fast anti-aliasing: smooths jagged edges on the finished picture. Cheap.
# Slightly softens fine detail. Presentation only, the guest does not change.
# Only in a window (ignored when headless, so captures stay unchanged).
#   true | false
# default: false
fxaa = false

# --- cas --------------------------------------------------------------------
# CAS sharpening (AMD FidelityFX CAS) on the finished picture, in percent.
# Pairs well with fxaa or a low scale. Presentation only, window only.
#   0 (off) to 100
# default: 0
cas = 0

# --- aniso ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Anisotropic filtering: keeps textures seen at a steep angle (the road going
# into the distance) sharp instead of blurry. Costs a little GPU.
# This changes rendered pixels (a host enhancement, not the stock look).
#   0 (off) | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16
# default: 0
aniso = 0

# --- mipmap -----------------------------------------------------------------
# PCSX2's emulation of the PS2's mipmaps (smaller texture copies used far
# away). On is what the real hardware does; off can shimmer or look wrong.
# Full mode only.
#   true | false
# default: true
mipmap = true



[input]
# --- analog -----------------------------------------------------------------
# true  : the controller is a DualShock 2: sticks steer, triggers have
#         pressure (the game's analog mode).
# false : a digital-only pad. The game ignores the sticks and trigger
#         pressure; steer with the d-pad.
# default: true
analog = true

# --- rumble -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Controller vibration, driven by the game like a DualShock 2. Only works with
# a controller that can rumble.
#   true | false
# default: true
rumble = true


[game]
# --- car_lod ----------------------------------------------------------------
# RR5 enhancement. Multiplies the game's car level-of-detail distances, so cars
# stay detailed farther away. Capped at the game's own cull distance.
# This changes guest data.
#   1        : stock game
#   a number : for example 2, 4, 6.5   (a decimal point is allowed)
# Do NOT use `best`; it overflows the game's display list and hangs a race.
# default: 4
car_lod = 4

# --- draw_distance ----------------------------------------------------------
# RR5 enhancement. The game draws the track's scenery from a baked list per
# course section, so far buildings pop in. This also draws the lists of the
# next N sections ahead, so they appear sooner. Costs speed: measured 107
# (stock) -> 89 (+2) -> 82 (+4) -> 68 (+8) frames/s unpaced at 4x; 2 is
# the sweet spot.
# This changes what the guest draws.
#   0        : stock game
#   1 to 16  : sections ahead
# default: 0
draw_distance = 0

# --- fast_unpack ------------------------------------------------------------
# RR5 enhancement. The game unpacks the data it loads from the disc on its
# main thread and draws nothing meanwhile, so the picture freezes (twice for
# about 1/3 s during the boot Namco logo). This runs the game's unpacker
# natively and nearly instantly: same data, no freeze, faster loading.
# This changes guest timing (not what is drawn).
#   true | false
# default: true
fast_unpack = true

# --- native_code ------------------------------------------------------------
# Host speed-up. The game's busiest functions (the 3D geometry builders and
# their helpers, about 30) run as native versions of their own recompiled
# code, with the game clock kept exactly: the guest sees the same state at
# every step, so the result is bit-for-bit the same, with less CPU used.
# Off runs all game code as plain recompiled code.
#   true | false
# default: true
native_code = true


[timing]
# --- unpaced ----------------------------------------------------------------
# false : real-time. Locks the game to 60000/1001 VBlanks per second
#         (about 59.94 Hz) and vsyncs the window (no tearing).
# true  : run as fast as the host can. For speed tests. No vsync.
# default: false
unpaced = false

# --- inline -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Where VIF1, VU1 and GS run.
#   false : on their own owner thread (faster; the default)
#   true  : on the EE thread, as before (for comparison and debugging)
# default: false
inline = false

# --- headless ---------------------------------------------------------------
# No window. For automated runs.
#   true | false
# default: false
headless = false

# --- from -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Replay debugging (with `replay` below). Run the first N VBlank starts as
# fast as the host can (sound muted), then switch to real time with vsync, so
# you land on a scene quickly and then watch it live. 60 starts = 1 second.
# Leave EMPTY for a normal launch. Needs unpaced = false.
# default: empty
from =


[paths]
# Advanced. Relative paths are relative to the repository root.
#
# runtime  : the packaged runtime NAME under runtime/ (not a path).
#            Leave EMPTY (recommended): the launcher uses the accepted product
#            runtime (game001-gate9-v142-5629843 today), and a newly accepted
#            runtime takes effect automatically, with no edit here.
#            Set a name only to pin an older runtime on purpose; that pins it
#            even after a new one is accepted.
# workload : folder holding your bound product workload.
#            default: local/gate3/product-live-v1
# replay   : a replay made from one of your sessions with
#              python3 scripts/make_replay.py local/product/sessions/<session> local/replays/<name>
#            It plays that session again, exactly, from its own copy of the
#            memory card (your saves are never touched). Your pad is ignored.
#            Use with `from` to jump to the moment you care about.
#            default: empty (a normal game)
# elf      : your own dumped game ELF. Normally EMPTY; the workload already
#            binds your disc. If set, it must be the exact ELF the workload
#            binds, or the launch is refused.
runtime =
workload = local/gate3/product-live-v1
replay =
elf =


[env]
# Advanced. Any line here is passed to the game as an environment variable, and
# is applied LAST, so it overrides what the settings above produce.
# Only names starting with RRV_ are accepted. One per line, NAME = value.
# Nothing is set by default. Examples (remove the leading # to use):
#
# Widescreen HUD scale, host side only (normally derived from ratio/hud):
#   RRV_PCSX2_GS_HUD_SCALE = 0.75
# Turn on the frontend diagnostics:
#   RRV_FRONTEND_DIAG = 1

unpaced = true
inline = true

cases.ini:
[display]
ratio = 21:9
hud = race
aspect = stretch
window = 1280x720
fullscreen = true
integer_scaling = true
present_pacing = false
[rendering]
render_mode = field
scale = 2
aa1 = false
fxaa = true
cas = 35
aniso = 16
mipmap = false
[input]
analog = false
rumble = false
[game]
car_lod = 1
draw_distance = 4
fast_unpack = false
native_code = false
[timing]
unpaced = true
inline = true
headless = true

errors.first_stderr_line: <INI>: line 2: window must be empty or WIDTHxHEIGHT, e.g. 1920x1080

errors.name: bad render_mode
errors.first_stderr_line: <INI>: line 2: render_mode must be full or field

errors.first_stderr_line: <INI>: line 2: cas must be 0 to 100 (0 = off)

errors.name: draw_distance 17

errors.name: unknown key
